memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you; do not sow and do not
reap what grows of itself or harvest the untended vines. For it is a
jubilee and is to be holy for you; eat only what is taken directly from
the fields'" - Lev 25:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Jubilee year followed straight after a Sabbath year. That meant two
consecutive years with no normal farming. Two years of trusting God for
food. This was an extraordinary call to depend on Him.

God was asking Israel to interrupt their entire economic cycle — not to
strive, not to accumulate, but to rest and receive. In a world that
measured security by stored grain, this was a radical act of faith.

Dear reader, our lives can become one long, unbroken cycle of producing
and consuming. Work, earn, spend, repeat. We rarely pause long enough to
ask whether we are trusting God or trusting our own output.

The Jubilee was holy — set apart, different from every other year. It
declared that human beings are more than their productivity, and that God
is the true source of security.

Jesus told of a man who tore down his barns to build bigger ones, planning
to store up years of ease — and God called him a fool, for that very
night his life was required of him (Luke 12:18-21). Accumulation is not
security.

You are not what you produce. Ask God to interrupt your cycle with a
holy pause, so you can remember where your true security lies.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has my life become an unbroken cycle of producing and consuming?
2. Do I measure my security by what I have stored up?
3. What holy pause could remind me that God is my provider?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, break the cycle in me that trusts in accumulation. Remind me that
my security is in You, not in what I store up. Amen.
